title: Enterprise Onboarding: Integration, Escalation, Health Checks & QBR Playbook
author: Aisha Khan
body:
Summary

This playbook consolidates the standard process for enterprise customer onboarding across integration, escalation handling, ongoing health checks, and Quarterly Business Reviews (QBRs). It is intended for Customer Success Engineers (CSEs), Solutions Engineers (SEs), Support on-call, and the Engineering on-call rotation.

Purpose & scope
- Ensure a repeatable, measurable onboarding experience for enterprise customers.
- Provide a single source of truth for integration checklist, escalation matrix, known issues/workarounds, and QBR/health-check cadence.
- Applies to all Dedicated and Private deployment customers, and to larger Hosted API accounts being migrated to enterprise support.

Audience
- CSEs, SEs, Support Engineers, Account Execs, Product Managers, and Eng SREs.

Quick links
- Integration templates: /confluence/eng-developer-experience/quickstarts-and-templates
- Runtime runbooks: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runbooks
- Incident process: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-process

1) Onboarding phases & timeline (recommended)
- Week 0 (Pre-sales handoff): contract + security questionnaire + initial kick-off. Owner: AM/CSE.
- Week 1 (Integration): API keys, auth, network allowlists, baseline traffic tests. Owner: SE.
- Week 2 (Validation): Model pinning, SLO alignment, latency/cost benchmarks, telemetry config. Owner: CSE/SE.
- Week 3 (Go-live prep): Canary routing, rate limiting, fallback policies, runbooks handed to customer ops. Owner: CSE/SRE.
- Week 4 (Go-live & stabilization): Monitor 72-hour burn-in, weekly health checks for first 30 days. Owner: CSE/SRE.

Onboarding timeline table (example)
- Column headers: Phase | Owner | Key deliverables | Acceptance criteria
- Pre-sales | AM/CSE | Contract, security answers | Security completed, SSO/KMS requirements documented
- Integration | SE | API keys, allowlists, test app | Successful test calls, 95th pct latency target validated
- Validation | CSE | Telemetry, model pins | Zero-critical errors, <1% 5xx, token cost baseline established

2) Integration checklist (minimum required items)
- Account & access
  1. Confirm account ID & billing contact.
  2. Create API key(s) scoped for environment and provide to customer via secure channel.
  3. Configure SSO/OAuth and verify with test user.
- Networking & security
  1. Provide IP ranges and domain names for allowlisting.
  2. Verify TLS/TCP connectivity and MTU when on-prem gateways are involved.
  3. KMS/HSM integration steps: verify key rotation and access policy.
- API & model configuration
  1. Verify model variant to be used (model name + version).
  2. Pin model version in config and document fallback variants.
  3. Confirm request/response schema and function/tool calling if used.
- Observability & telemetry
  1. Ensure logging endpoints and log retention settings are agreed.
  2. Enable per-route tracing and token-level cost reporting for first 30 days.
  3. Add customer to the CSE monitoring dashboard and grant read access.
- Performance validation
  1. Run baseline load tests: 1k warm requests, synthetic traces at target seq lengths.
  2. Capture p50/p95/p99 latency, 5xx rate, CPU/GPU utilization.
  3. Agree on SLOs and error budgets (see SLO section).

3) Service Level Objectives (SLOs) and targets (recommended defaults)
- Availability: 99.9% monthly for Dedicated customers.
- Latency: p95 <= 300 ms for short-text generation (<=128 tokens) under steady load.
- Error rate: 5xx <= 0.5% sustained.
- Support response targets (for incidents): see Escalation matrix below.

4) Escalation matrix & incident flow
Severity definitions (customer-facing)
- P0 (Critical): Production outage causing total loss of inference traffic or data corruption.
- P1 (High): Severe degradation (latency > 2x SLO or error rate > 5%) impacting >10% of requests.
- P2 (Medium): Partial degradation impacting specific routes/features or intermittent errors.
- P3 (Low): Minor issues, configuration questions, or enhancement requests.

Response and restoration targets
- P0: initial response <= 15 minutes, escalation to Eng on-call within 30 minutes, restore/mitigation action within 2 hours (or provide mitigation).
- P1: initial response <= 1 hour, mitigation plan within 4 hours, restore within 24 hours (or rolling mitigation).
- P2: initial response <= 8 business hours, workaround or plan in 3 business days.
- P3: initial response <= 2 business days.

Escalation steps (numbered procedure)
1. Customer reports issue to support@redwood.ai or opens ticket in the portal. Support triages and assigns severity.
2. If P0/P1, page on-call via PagerDuty using the customer-specific escalation policy. Include incident summary, customer ID, and recent logs.
3. On-call acknowledges within response SLA and runs the customer runbook. If not resolved in the first 30 minutes (P0) escalate to Eng-SRE primary and CSE lead.
4. Use the incident template: Impact, Scope, Hypothesis, Mitigation, Next steps. Post updates every 15-30 minutes for P0 until mitigated.
5. After restoration, create a postmortem within 72 hours (see /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/postmortems).

Escalation contacts (examples)
- Customer Success (CSE): cse-oncall@redwood.ai (primary daytime)
- Support Pager: support-pager@redwood.ai (PagerDuty)
- Eng-SRE on-call: see /confluence/eng-sre/roster (link)
- Account Executive: listed in customer record (Salesforce link)

5) Runbook checklist & triage commands
- Information to collect on first triage:
  - Customer ID, environment (prod/stage), exact timestamps, API key used, recent call-id(s).
  - p95 latency, 5xx rate in last 5m/1h, GPU utilization, queue depth.
- Useful queries and commands:
  - check recent 5xx: curl -X GET "https://observability.internal/api/metrics?customer_id=<id>&metric=5xx_rate&window=5m"
  - get p95 latency: query the metrics service: METRICS.q("latency.p95", {customer_id: "<id>", window: "1h"})
  - collect logs for call-id: logs tail --customer <id> --callid <callid> --since 15m > /tmp/cust123.log
  - restart customer router: kubectl rollout restart deployment/customer-router-<id> -n customer-prod (Eng approval required)
- Common immediate mitigations:
  1. Failover to fallback model variant or region (if configured).
  2. Enable stricter rate-limiting for the customer to prevent overload.
  3. Re-route to Dedicated burst pool or suspend nonessential background tasks.

6) Known issues & workarounds (selected)
- Issue: Large-context KV cache eviction causing occasional latency spikes.
  - Symptoms: p95 latency increases at sequence length > 4096; increased CUDA memory activity.
  - Workaround: Temporarily reduce max_sequence length to 3072 and enable prefix caching. Owner: Runtime team (eng-serving-runtime).
- Issue: Intermittent 502s for customers behind older on-prem proxies.
  - Symptoms: 502 responses correlated to proxy TLS renegotiation.
  - Workaround: Advise customer to upgrade proxy to TLS 1.2+ and increase keepalive. Short-term: route traffic through a regional gateway. Owner: Eng-Infra.
- Issue: Token cost spikes after model upgrade (unexpected prompt engineering change).
  - Symptoms: Cost per 1k tokens baseline doubles after model switch.
  - Workaround: Roll back to previous model pin while CSE engages Applied ML to review prompt differences. Owner: Applied ML and CSE.

7) Health checks & QBR template
Health check cadence (first 30 days)
- Daily automated checks during first 72 hours: error rate, p95 latency, traffic volume, cost anomalies.
- Weekly check-ins during month 1: CSE review of telemetry and customer feedback.
- Monthly after stabilization: standard health check.

QBR template (recommended slides/sections)
1. Executive summary: adoption, business impact, top wins/risks.
2. Usage & adoption: Monthly Active Routes, peak concurrency, average tokens per month.
3. Reliability & performance: availability %, p95 latency, 5xx rate, incidents since last QBR.
4. Cost & efficiency: cost per 1k tokens, batching/caching saving opportunities, recommendations.
5. Roadmap & requests: planned model upgrades, required integrations, upcoming maintenance windows.
6. Action items & owner matrix.

Metrics to surface in health checks
- Active routes, tokens/month, p95 latency, availability, 5xx rate, cost per 1k tokens, average batch size, KV cache hit rate.

8) Handoff & sign-off checklist
- Confirm: all integration checklist items completed and signed off.
- Confirm: SLOs agreed and reflected in contract (if enterprise).
- Confirm: CSE has knowledge transfer session recorded and runbooks shared.
- Sign-off required from: Customer Admin + Redwood CSE + SE.

9) Postmortems, continuous improvement & feedback loop
- Postmortems required for P0/P1 incidents with customer impact. Include impact assessment and remediation plans.
- Maintain a triage log of recurring issues; escalate recurring patterns to Runtime or Infra teams for engineering fixes.
- Quarterly review of onboarding playbook and checklist items; update if >2 customers report friction in same area.

10) Contacts & ownership (examples)
- CSE Lead: Aisha Khan (aisha@redwood.ai)
- Support Manager: Tom Lefevre (tom@redwood.ai)
- Eng-SRE Pager: see /confluence/eng-sre/roster
- Runtime escalation owner: Maya Chen (maya@redwood.ai)

Change log
- 2026-04-15: Initial draft and pre-release for pilots.
- 2026-05-20: Published with updated SLOs and known-issues section (post pilot changes).

Appendix: Templates & artifacts
- Integration checklist (copyable): https://internal-templates.redwood.ai/integration-checklist
- Incident status template: https://internal-templates.redwood.ai/incident-template
- QBR slide deck template: https://internal-templates.redwood.ai/qbr-template

If you are onboarding a customer now, follow the Integration checklist step-by-step, schedule the first-week performance validation, and add the customer to the CSE monitoring dashboard. For any escalation ambiguity, page Eng-SRE immediately and notify the CSE lead.
